cards.front: What is the minimum number of registered principals that a non-sole-proprietorship member firm must employ?
cards.back: At least two registered principals.

cards.front: List the primary supervisory duties of a registered principal.
cards.back: Accepting/approving new accounts; approving margin and options accounts; approving or reviewing communications; reviewing trading activity; hiring and training new representatives; responding to written customer complaints.

cards.front: Customer Complaint (FINRA definition)
cards.back: A written statement by a customer (or someone acting on the customer's behalf) alleging a grievance arising out of, or in connection with, a securities transaction. Includes electronic communications.

cards.front: How often must a member firm report written complaints to FINRA, and how long must complaint records be retained?
cards.back: A report listing all written complaints must be filed with FINRA within 15 days of the end of each calendar quarter. Copies of complaints must be held for 4 years after resolution.

cards.front: Who at the member firm must handle a written customer complaint?
cards.back: A registered principal. All written complaints must be routed to a principal for action.

cards.front: What are the two components of FINRA's continuing education (CE) requirement?
cards.back: The Firm Element and the Regulatory Element.

cards.front: Who must receive Firm Element CE training, and by when each year?
cards.back: All registered persons who have direct contact with the public. It must be completed by December 31 each year (the firm may set an earlier deadline). Failure may result in suspension of the representative's license.

cards.front: What factors must a firm consider when developing its annual Firm Element training plan?
cards.back: Recent regulatory developments, the scope of the firm's business activities, the performance of personnel in the Regulatory Element, and the firm's training needs.

cards.front: When must registered persons complete the Regulatory Element of continuing education?
cards.back: Within 120 days of the person's 2nd registration anniversary, and every 3 years thereafter (5th, 8th, 11th, etc.).

cards.front: What happens if a registered person fails to complete the Regulatory Element within the required time?
cards.back: FINRA will deactivate that person's registration until the requirements of the program are met.

cards.front: Who determines the content of the Regulatory Element of CE?
cards.back: FINRA. The content is tailored to whether the person holds RR or principal status.

cards.front: Outside Business Activity (OBA)
cards.back: Any activity for compensation outside the scope of an associated person's relationship with the member firm. Prior written notice to the employing member is required (regardless of whether the firm approves).

cards.front: An RR plans to teach evening business and finance classes at a local community college for pay. What must she do under FINRA rules?
cards.back: She must provide prior written notice to her employing broker-dealer before engaging in the outside business activity, because the activity is for compensation outside her work with the firm.

cards.front: An RR volunteers as a coach for her son's little league with no compensation. Must she notify her employing BD?
cards.back: No. Because there is no compensation involved, prior written notice as an outside business activity is not required.

cards.front: Private Securities Transaction (Selling Away)
cards.back: Any sale of securities outside an associated person's regular business and her employing member firm.

cards.front: What must an associated person do before engaging in a private securities transaction?
cards.back: Provide prior written notice to the employer; describe in detail the proposed transaction; describe her proposed role; and disclose whether she will receive compensation.

cards.front: How are compensated private securities transactions treated by the employing member firm if approved?
cards.back: The firm must record the transaction on its own books and supervise the associated person as if the firm itself were conducting the trade. If disapproved, the associated person may not participate.

cards.front: How are non-compensated private securities transactions handled by the employer?
cards.back: The firm must acknowledge receipt of written notification and may impose conditions on participation — including outright prohibition.

cards.front: Which private securities transactions are excluded from the definition entirely?
cards.back: Transactions the associated person enters into on behalf of immediate family members for which no compensation is received.

cards.front: What is the current annual dollar limit on gifts and gratuities to employees of other member firms?
cards.back: $100 per person per year. The gift cannot be conditioned on sales and must have the employing member's prior approval.

cards.front: What types of gifts/expenditures are exempt from the $100 annual gift limit?
cards.back: Occasional noncash items (dinners, seminars, entertainment tickets); reminder advertising items bearing the firm's logo (pens, mouse pads); and items given for life events (weddings, birth of a child, retirement).

cards.front: A mutual fund wholesaler takes two RRs to dinner twice a year costing $400-$500 to discuss new funds. Is this a violation of the $100 gift limit?
cards.back: No. Because it is occasional and the wholesaler is present discussing business, it qualifies as allowable business entertainment, not a gift.

cards.front: A mutual fund wholesaler sends an RR season tickets (worth ~$2,000) for the RR's favorite team, with no plan to attend. Is this permitted?
cards.back: No. This is a violation because it is not occasional, the wholesaler is not present, and no business is being discussed. It exceeds the $100 gift limit.

cards.front: MSRB Rule G-37 (Pay-to-Play)
cards.back: Prohibits municipal securities firms from engaging in negotiated municipal securities business or financial advisory work with an issuer for 2 years after a political contribution is made to an official of that issuer by the firm, an MFP, or a firm-controlled PAC.

cards.front: What types of municipal business does MSRB Rule G-37 specifically target?
cards.back: Negotiated underwritings (where the issuer selects the underwriter) and financial advisory work. It does not apply to competitive bid underwritings.

cards.front: Municipal Finance Professional (MFP)
cards.back: An associated person of a FINRA member engaged in municipal securities underwriting, trading, sales, financial advisory, research, or investment advice involving communication with public investors. Excludes those limited to retail sales to individuals or clerical/ministerial work.

cards.front: What is the de minimis political contribution exemption under MSRB Rule G-37?
cards.back: An MFP may contribute up to $250 per election to a candidate for whom the MFP is eligible to vote without triggering the 2-year ban. The exemption does NOT apply to contributions from the firm itself.

cards.front: Which regulator enforces MSRB rules, including Rule G-37?
cards.back: FINRA. The MSRB writes the rules but has no enforcement authority.

cards.front: A municipal firm made a political contribution to a city official 1 year ago. The city is now issuing new bonds via competitive bid. May the firm participate?
cards.back: Yes. MSRB Rule G-37's 2-year ban applies only to negotiated underwritings and financial advisory work — not to competitive bid underwritings.
